claims.statement: Brijio is operated through a single combined binary (bin/brijio.mjs, published as dist/bin/brijio.js) that starts both the WebSocket relay and the MCP HTTP server in one process, auto-generates tokens, and installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers for graceful shutdown of both servers.

The brijio CLI parses process.argv into a DaemonCommand via parseDaemonCommand in daemon.ts; top-level flags (--help/-h, --print-config, --doctor, --version) are handled before subcommands, --dev is extracted so it never reaches server args, and unknown first tokens fall through to run mode as interactive server args.

The brijio CLI subcommand surface is run (default), demo, print-config [agent], doctor, install [--ws-port --mcp-port], uninstall, start, stop, restart, status, logs [--lines --live], and help, plus top-level --dev and --version flags, as documented by usage() in daemon.ts.

loadBrijioEnv resolves a .env file from candidates in order — BRIJIO_ENV_FILE override, <cwd>/.env, then ~/.brijio/.env — using the first that exists; applyBrijioEnv copies loaded values into process.env only for keys that are unset or empty, so real environment variables always take precedence over .env values.

Backward-compatible env aliases are accepted during the transition: BRIJIO_PAIRING_TOKEN accepts BROWSERBRIDGE_PAIRING_TOKEN/BRIJIO_TOKEN, BRIJIO_WS_URL accepts BROWSERBRIDGE_WEBSOCKET_URL/BRIJIO_WEBSOCKET_URL/WEBSOCKET_URL, BRIJIO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS accepts BROWSERBRIDGE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, and BRIJIO_BROWSER_INSTANCE_ID accepts BROWSERBRIDGE_BROWSER_INSTANCE_ID; when both new and old names are set with different values the new name is preferred and a warning is emitted.

Auto-generated tokens are produced with crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') and are ephemeral — they change on every restart unless persisted; the startup banner labels them [ephemeral] and the daemon install command persists them to ~/.brijio/.env.

The MCP server's approvalTimeoutMs is not configured directly but derived as Math.max(1000, httpTimeoutMs - approvalTimeoutBufferMs), where httpTimeoutMs comes from BRIJIO_MCP_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS (default 60000) and approvalTimeoutBufferMs from BRIJIO_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_BUFFER_MS (default 5000), with a 1000ms floor preventing collapse.

Both servers expose GET /health (ADR 0033): the WebSocket relay returns status/version/uptimeSeconds plus an extensions object with the count and list of connected browser instances from its in-memory presence table, while the MCP HTTP server returns status/version/uptimeSeconds plus a websocket object with the configured WS URL and a reachability status reported as 'unknown' on probe failure rather than blocking the response.

Both servers log structured single-line JSON to stderr via the shared createLogger from @brijio/shared, with timestamp, level, message, service name, and arbitrary fields, so logs never interfere with MCP stdio transport or HTTP response pipes and work with docker logs and journalctl.

brijio --doctor runs preflight checks (config file presence, MCP and WebSocket port availability, network detection, Node.js version >= 18) and exits 1 if any check has status fail, 0 otherwise; warnings do not fail the exit code.

brijio --print-config [agent] emits a ready-to-copy MCP client config block to stdout and a where-to-paste hint to stderr, with per-agent formatters for claude-desktop/cursor/cline (mcpServers JSON), vscode (servers JSON), codex/claude-code/gemini (shell commands), hermes (YAML), windsurf (env interpolation), zed (context_servers), continue (YAML), and goose (instructional note that HTTP requires a bridge), resolving names and aliases via resolveAgentName and presenting an interactive picker on a TTY when no agent is given.

The startup banner is written to stderr so stdout stays clean for piping; it shows reachable WS/MCP URL pairs per detected network address (Tailscale/mDNS/localhost) in non-dev mode or a single localhost pair in dev mode, the pairing and MCP auth tokens marked [ephemeral] when auto-generated with a persistence warning, a dev-mode indicator, and the demo page URL in demo mode.

brijio demo (ADR 0039) starts the full WS(8787)+MCP(8788)+demo page(8789) stack for self-contained tool verification with no Docker or extension, binding WS/MCP to 127.0.0.1 for security and the demo static server to 0.0.0.0; if a daemon is already running on the WS port it attaches to it and starts only the demo server to avoid port conflicts and pairing-token scope mismatches.

The demo static server resolves its file root from BRIJIO_DEMO_DIR override, a walk-up search for clients/test-page/index.html (monorepo dev), then a demo/ folder (npm bundled dist/demo), then <cwd>/clients/test-page, with a default port of 8789 (BRIJIO_DEMO_PORT, alias BROWSERBRIDGE_DEMO_PORT) and path-traversal guards.

The daemon install model (ADR 0037) supports macOS (LaunchAgent label com.redvex.brijio, symlinked to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/) and Linux (systemd user unit brijio.service, symlinked to ~/.config/systemd/user/), storing config and generated tokens in ~/.brijio/.env with mode 0600; the plist/unit sets WorkingDirectory to ~/.brijio so the daemon always finds its .env, and the macOS plist uses RunAtLoad/KeepAlive true with stdout/stderr redirected to ~/.brijio/brijio.log.

Daemon install is idempotent: if ~/.brijio/.env already exists it preserves existing tokens and only fills missing ones, while new --ws-port/--mcp-port flags override existing WEBSOCKET_PORT/MCP_HTTP_PORT values; uninstall stops the daemon and removes the service link but preserves ~/.brijio/.env and logs, printing 'rm -rf ~/.brijio' for full removal.

Daemon lifecycle commands wrap platform service managers: macOS uses launchctl load/unload on the link while Linux uses systemctl --user start/stop/restart/enable/daemon-reload brijio.service; logs tails ~/.brijio/brijio.log on macOS (tail -n/-f) and journalctl --user -u brijio.service on Linux.

brijio status loads ~/.brijio/.env for ports, checks whether the daemon is loaded (macOS launchctl list com.redvex.brijio; Linux systemctl --user is-active --quiet), then probes http://127.0.0.1:<wsPort>/health and http://127.0.0.1:<mcpPort>/health with a 1500ms timeout each and prints a table of daemon loaded, config path, binary path, and WebSocket/MCP health.

Docker (ADR 0035) ships as a single combined image running both services under s6-overlay, where docker/s6-rc.d/brijio/run execs node dist/bin/brijio.js so the same token auto-generation and banner logic applies; the image EXPOSEs 8787 and 8788 with ENTRYPOINT /init and the MCP server connects to ws://127.0.0.1:8787 since both processes share the container network namespace.

Inside Docker, 127.0.0.1 binding does not work with port mapping because it binds only the container loopback unreachable from the host even with -p; the intended security boundary for Docker is the 0.0.0.0 default plus auth tokens, or docker run --network=host with 127.0.0.1 binding for strictly local access.

docker-compose.yml defines services behind profiles: brijio (profile runtime, exposing 8787 and 8788), browserbridge (extends brijio, profile legacy-runtime), and test-page (nginx serving clients/test-page, profile test on TEST_PAGE_PORT default 8080); per AGENTS.md the current profiles must be derived from docker-compose.yml and not assumed to exist.
